description: This case study is the main report of the Fifth Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment for Ukraine, covering February 2022 to December 2025 and released in February 2026 by the Government of Ukraine, the World Bank Group, the European Commission and the United Nations (76 pages). It gives damage, loss and needs by sector; the energy and extractives page covers electricity generation, transmission and distribution, gas systems, district heating networks, oil facilities and coal mining, and reports damage of 24.8 billion US dollars, loss of 88.2 billion and needs of 90.6 billion, with generation the largest damaged component. The report adds recovery priorities for 2026 and cross-cutting areas for resilient reconstruction, and reports that repeated long power outages in late 2025 hit millions of consumers. Access: free PDF; reproduction is allowed for noncommercial purposes with attribution. Coverage is Ukraine nationally, with oblast-level concentration only described in text. Caveats: only the front matter and the energy overview page were read here, and the estimates rest on government data and a stated methodology in Annex 1. It suits resilience and capacity planning studies of grids under sustained attack, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

name: Ukraine Fifth Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment, RDNA5 main report: energy and extractives damage, loss and needs (February 2022 to December 2025)
outcomes: For energy and extractives the report estimates damage of 24.8 billion US dollars, war-related loss of 88.2 billion and recovery and reconstruction needs of 90.6 billion as of 30 November 2025. The power subsector holds about 70 percent of damage (17.1 billion, of which generation 14.2 billion, transmission 2.3 billion and distribution 0.7 billion), concentrated in Zaporizka, Kharkivska, Kirovohradska, Dnipropetrovska, Donetska and Odeska oblasts and Kyiv. Power needs are 70.8 billion; priorities include decentralised generation, renewables, flexible capacity, physical protection of critical assets and passing the heating season.
